USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our tariff posture and use the agreed Trump-Xi meeting at the Buenos Aires G-20 next month as the venue to press for concrete concessions on structural IP and technology-transfer, without pre-committing to any rollback and without escalating the list further this cycle. Do not raise new tariffs now — markets are brittle and the farm-belt midterm base is already absorbing retaliation — and do not concede, since we retain escalation dominance and China is the one feeling the pain.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat to US interests is modest and net-negative: we initiated the dispute, hold escalation dominance (Section 301 coverage of ~$250B vs China's ~$60-77B retaliation per the Sept 24 entries), and the US macro economy remains strong through it — industrial production up ~1.5% since April, consumer sentiment ~98.6, the dollar up ~4.8%, and CPI contained near 0.8% (country_health). That is the -0.25 reading: a mild opportunity, not a clear one. The offsetting costs are real and visible at the decision date: the Dow fell 831 points on Oct 10 in the worst session in eight months, with the S&P down ~5% from its peak, attributed partly to the trade war plus rising rates (10-year at a seven-year high of ~3.2%, Baa yields up to 5.07%) — evidence the dispute is now feeding financial fragility and could bite via credit and equity channels. The diplomatic track is the operative fact: Trump and Xi have agreed to meet at the G-20 in Buenos Aires (WaPo, Oct 11; Kudlow, Oct 5), our first direct leader talks since August, creating an off-ramp. Given that off-ramp plus the Nov 6 midterms and fragile markets, escalating further would harden Beijing's position and feed the sell-off while surrender would waste leverage; negotiating from our position of strength is the disciplined move.
key_factors: US holds escalation dominance (~$250B Section 301 coverage vs China's ~$60-77B retaliation; Sept 24 timeline entries)
US economy strong through dispute: IP +1.5%, sentiment 98.6, dollar +4.8%, CPI contained (~0.8%)
October equity selloff (Dow -831 Oct 10; S&P -5% from peak) partly attributed to trade war + rising rates
10-yr Treasury at 7-year high (~3.2%) and Baa yield at 5.07% signal tightening financial conditions
Trump-Xi meeting agreed at G-20 Buenos Aires (end Nov) — first leader-level talks since August
Jan 1, 2019 scheduled rise of List 3 from 10% to 25% retains credible leverage
Nov 6 midterms + farm-belt soybean retaliation create domestic political sensitivity

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5-10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping have agreed to meet next month at the G-20 summit in Buenos Aires in hopes of resolving their intensifying trade conflict.
Dow falls 831 points (3.1%), Nasdaq >4%, fifth consecutive daily decline for S&P; selling driven by rising bond yields plus fears of escalating China trade tensions.
US IP +1.5% since May; 10-yr to 3.19%; broad dollar +4.8%; consumer sentiment 98.6; Baa corporate yield to 5.07%.
